scope: The forks AND the harbour: the Chicago River from the North and South Branches at Wolf Point east down the main stem, through the 1834 cut, past the sand bar and the decaying old southward channel, to open Lake Michigan — and, since T-1123, the North Branch above the forks to the north line of Wright's survey. Land is the three divisions the river separates, the Fort Dearborn reservation, the lakeshore sand-ridge belt east of State Street, the North Division ground Kinzie's Addition is platted on, and the bar itself.
standard: No contour survey of the 1835 town site exists. The earliest systematic levels are the 1850s street-grade and Chesbrough sewerage surveys. Every land elevation below is a period narrative statement in feet, back-calculated from grade-raising records, or inferred from geology — so NO land elevation in this spec is better than 'inferred', and the generator refuses to emit a 'documented' confidence for any land vertex. The one documented surface is the water: the pre-reversal river was sluggish and outward-flowing with a near-zero surface gradient, standing at lake level through the whole downtown reach.

notes: The offshore lake bed, which the dossier tags conjectural outright: slope about 1:60 to 1:100, -10 ft at 600-1000 ft offshore. A -11 ft bed with a 130 m e-fold reproduces that band — about -8.7 ft at 200 m (656 ft) offshore and about -4 ft at 60 m — using the same law as every other reach rather than a second one. Three anchors down the box's east side, because one would let the old channel's -2.5 ft bleed into the lake south-east of the bar. STILL THREE after T-1123 put 720 m of new open lake north of the harbour, and that was a measurement rather than an omission: three more up the east side moved 52 000 samples of the committed field, most of them under the town's own main stem, because the bed blend's support is unbounded. Without them the new northern rows fall 1:25 to 1:30 over the first 25 m and reach -9.7 ft some 370 m offshore, which is the same shape as the committed rows south of the harbour (1:10 to 1:25 at the beach, -9.4 ft at 320 m) and inside dossier zone 30's band. The blend already answers for this water; nothing needed adding to make it. Nobody sounded this water for this project and nobody sounded it in 1835; it is here so the harbour opens into a lake instead of into a wall.

notes: Dossier zone 21 gives -6 to -10 ft for the branch beds above the forks, itself inferred. Midpoint taken. ONE ANCHOR, AND T-1123 TRIED NINE AND WITHDREW THEM. The northern extension carries about 320 m of this branch into the box above the forks, and nine mid-channel anchors up the traced polygon looked like the obvious way to keep the main stem's -12 ft out of it. Measured, they moved 11 405 samples of the committed field that the extension had no business moving — the bed is an inverse-square blend with unbounded support, so an anchor placed 700 m up a branch pulls on the town's own river — while the single anchor already models the new stretch at -6.5 ft mid-channel at N +500, inside zone 21's own range. Withdrawn on that measurement.

THE FORT'S RIVER FRONTAGE STANDS STEEPER THAN THE BANKS EITHER SIDE OF IT, and it has to: the traced 1834 waterline runs 4.5 m north of the stockade's north-west corner and 7 m north of its north-east corner, while the reach's own 20 m face needs four times that distance to bring ground to full height. Built at 20 m the ramp reached some 15 m INSIDE the fort and scaled the north wall's ground to 1.26 m against the parade's 3.65 m, sinking a twelve-foot stockade to four feet of visible picket (T-0125, on the owner's ruling of 2026-08-21 that the ground gives rather than the bake or the placement).
